newsitem.title: USA: CBOT March wheat sets new contract low, recovers.
newsitem.headline: CBOT March wheat sets new contract low, recovers.

text.p: CBOT March wheat set a new contract low early on persistent reminders of the large supply of wheat worldwide amid only routine export business, traders said.
The new low for March was $3.51 per bushel as of 1044 CST, below the previous low of $3.52 posted Monday.

Traders and analysts have said USDA in its February supply/demand report slated for release at 0730 CST Wednesday may increase its estimate for the Australian wheat crop. Some expect USDA to hike its outlook for Australia's crop by one million tonnes.
USDA in January estimated Australia's crop at 21.5 million tonnes. The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) pegged the crop at 23.226 million tonnes.
Trading was muted before the release Wednesday of the government's updated figures for the U.S. grains balance sheet.
"Everybody is waiting for tomorrow," a trader said.
At 1100 CST, wheat was 1/4 to one cent per bushel higher, with March up 1/4 at $3.52-3/4.
New crop July was firm relative to the March and at 1100 CST was up one at $3.40-1/2.
